title: Ezra 4
paragraphs: ¹ When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel, ² they came to Zerubbabel and the family heads and said, "Let us help you build. Like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here." ³ But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the family heads of Israel answered them, "You have no part with us in building a temple to our God. We alone will build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, just as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, commanded us." ⁴ Then the peoples around them set out to discourage the people of Judah and make them afraid to build. ⁵ They hired counselors to work against them and frustrate their plans throughout the entire reign of Cyrus king of Persia and down to the reign of Darius king of Persia.

⁶ At the beginning of the reign of Ahasuerus, the adversaries lodged a written accusation against the people of Judah and Jerusalem. ⁷ And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their associates wrote a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic script and translated into Aramaic. ⁸ Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes about Jerusalem. It said: ⁹ Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the secretary, together with their associates — the judges and officials of the Dinaites, Apharsathchites, Tarpelites, Apharsites, Archevites, Babylonians, Susanchites, Dehavites, Elamites, ¹⁰ and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Ashurbanipal deported and settled in the city of Samaria and elsewhere in the province beyond the Euphrates — hereby write:

¹¹ This is a copy of the letter they sent to Artaxerxes the king: To King Artaxerxes, from your servants in the region beyond the Euphrates. ¹² Let the king know that the Jews who came up from you to us have gone to Jerusalem and are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They are restoring its walls and repairing its foundations. ¹³ Furthermore, let the king know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, these people will stop paying taxes, tribute, and duty, and the royal treasury will suffer. ¹⁴ Because we are loyal to the palace and it would not be right for us to sit by while the king's honor is at stake, we have sent word to inform the king ¹⁵ so that a search may be made in the records of your predecessors. You will find in those records that this city is a rebellious city — troublesome to kings and provinces, a place with a long history of sedition. That is why it was destroyed.

¹⁶ We want the king to know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls restored, you will have no province left in the region beyond the Euphrates. ¹⁷ The king sent this reply to Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the secretary, and the rest of their associates living in Samaria and elsewhere in the province beyond the Euphrates: Greetings. ¹⁸ The letter you sent to me has been carefully read and translated in my presence. ¹⁹ I issued an order and a search was made, and it was found that this city has a long history of revolt against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been carried on there. ²⁰ Jerusalem has had powerful kings who ruled over the whole province beyond the Euphrates, and taxes, tribute, and duty were paid to them.

²¹ Therefore, issue an order that these men must stop work, so that this city is not rebuilt until I so order. ²² Be careful not to neglect this matter. Why let this threat grow, to the detriment of the royal interests? ²³ As soon as the copy of the letter from King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, Shimshai the secretary, and their associates, they went immediately to the Jews in Jerusalem and compelled them to stop by force of arms. ²⁴ So the work on the house of God in Jerusalem came to a standstill. And it remained stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
